original_question: Give a rigorous mathematical definition of averaging in general relativity that is suitable for coarse graining geometry and matter on a curved spacetime.
target_in_paper: Section 5.3, Problem PF2: "Provide a rigorous mathematical definition for averaging in GR."
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies that the issue is a definition problem in general relativity, and it captures the nearby motivation that averaging is meant to support coarse graining of geometry and matter on curved spacetime. This matches the official open problem PF2 in §5.3 rather than the distinct follow-up problem PF3 about cosmological significance and the maximal coarse-graining scale.
missing_details: The paper frames the problem as one of spacetime or space-volume averaging, not just informal coarse graining.
The definition should be mathematically rigorous in a differential-geometric setting: averaging tensors on a differential manifold is part of the stated context.
The averaging procedure should be well posed.
It should be generally covariant (and, in the macroscopic-gravity discussion, gauge independent), reflecting GR’s coordinate freedom.

The ambient setting should be made explicit: in the paper’s GR background, one works on a smooth (or sufficiently differentiable) 4-dimensional Lorentz manifold (M, g), with Einstein’s equations coupled in general to matter fields.
The goal is not merely to average quantities numerically, but to obtain a macroscopic/averaged geometry and macroscopic matter fields.

Because Einstein’s equations are nonlinear, the averaged field equations need not have the same mathematical form as the original equations; a faithful formulation should leave room for additional correlation terms.

The paper distinguishes this definition problem (PF2) from the separate PF3 question asking whether averaging plays an important role in cosmology and what the largest admissible coarse-graining scale is.
No algebraic data such as ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, quantification over large m, or similar parameters occur in this paper; those template items are inapplicable here.
refined_question: On a smooth 4-dimensional Lorentz manifold (M,g) in general relativity, provide a mathematically rigorous definition of spacetime or space-volume averaging that is well posed and generally covariant, applies to the tensorial geometric and matter fields on the underlying differential manifold, and yields well-defined macroscopic geometry and macroscopic matter fields together with corresponding averaged gravitational field equations, without assuming a priori that the averaged equations retain the exact form of the local Einstein equations and with any correlation terms arising from nonlinearity made explicit.
justification: The draft is best matched to Problem PF2 in §5.3, whose official wording is exactly about giving a rigorous mathematical definition of averaging in GR. I did not replace it by PF3, because PF3 is a different, downstream question about whether averaging is cosmologically important and about the largest scale of coarse graining compatible with exact Einstein evolution. I sharpened the draft only by importing the adjacent paper-defined constraints and scope: averaging should be well posed and generally covariant; it concerns tensors on a differential manifold; it is motivated by deriving large-scale/macroscopic geometry and matter fields from local GR; and the nonlinear nature of Einstein’s equations means correlation terms may appear and the averaged equations need not preserve the microscopic form. The paper has no Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3, so those prioritization instructions are not applicable to this arXiv ID.
